CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFINCLUDE

CFINCLUDE reads another template and runs it right where the tag stands. The included template shares the Variables scope of the page that includes it, so it can read and set the page's variables. It is the easy way to share headers, footers and common code between pages.

Category

Flow control

Syntax

<CFINCLUDE TEMPLATE="template_name">

Attributes

TEMPLATE
Required. Path of the template to include. A relative path is taken from the directory of the current template (../footer.cfm works). A path starting with / goes through the mappings on the Administrator's Mappings page; the / mapping points to the web root.

Usage

Paired tags must start and end in the same file: you cannot open a CFIF or CFOUTPUT in one template and close it in the included one. If the template cannot be found, a MissingInclude error is raised; CFCATCH.MissingFileName names the file.

Unlike a custom tag called with CFMODULE, an included template gets no Attributes scope and no private variables of its own. Choose CFINCLUDE for shared page fragments and a custom tag for reusable components.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- sn_pagetitle.cfm draws a title bar from Variables.PageTitle,
      and sets Variables.TitleDrawn for the including page to use --->
<CFSET PageTitle = "Quarterly Parks Report">
<CFINCLUDE TEMPLATE="sn_pagetitle.cfm">

<CFQUERY NAME="Parks" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT ParkName, State FROM Parks WHERE Region = 'Southwest' ORDER BY ParkName
</CFQUERY>
<UL>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Parks"><LI>#ParkName# (#State#)</CFOUTPUT>
</UL>

<CFSET PageTitle = "Appendix: No Parks Were Harmed">
<CFINCLUDE TEMPLATE="sn_pagetitle.cfm">
<CFOUTPUT><P>The include file has drawn #TitleDrawn# title bars on this page.</P></CFOUTPUT>
